  • Cut negative people out of my life without a second thought (this makes people think I'm shallow or cold, yet those that have stuck with me and been with me through shit know that if they ever need anything I will put my dick away mid-stream and come help them)

  • Emotional control. I feel just like anyone else, but I can control my emotions. If you play with your cards facing out then you're going to lose the game every time. It's not about manipulation, as some would have you believe, it's about not being manipulative. This seems counter-intuitive but when you think about it, does your approach to a person change depending on the signals they give out? Would you approach a person who is crying and say 'Hey, beautiful day isn't it?' or would you walk up and talk to them in a soppy voice "Hey, what's wrong? Can I help?'. I know which one I'd prefer, and that is to not bother other people with my problems. As soon as your emotions are display other peoples actions and reactions are modified to compensate. If you are having a shit day you should be able to say it like a man 'Hey mate, yeah it's a gorgeous day. I'm in a bit of a rut today and just having some time to myself.'

  • Minimalising responsibility. Not in the sense that I have less responsibility, but that to me my responsibilities are a small factor in my life. This is one all my friends complain about. Got to do this, got to do that. Blah blah blah. If you manage your time, money and relationships without taking on more shit than you can handle then suddenly responsibilities don't seem like a hill you have to climb but a bump that you can deal with in no time. The biggest one I see people struggle with is bills. Really it's not too hard. Calculate all your expenses for a year based on an average, add 10%, then divide the total by the number of pay weeks you have in a year. That number is the amount you automatically transfer to a 'responsibility' account that has no cards or anything attached. Then when bills come they are always covered. This also means you don't have to look at your spending account and think 'Oh, but I've got a bill that'll be due soon maybe I can't go out for drinks' because all the money in that account is there to be enjoyed.

  • Savings. I said earlier that I buy and do what I want without concern for money, and don't have a huge stockpile of cash. That doesn't mean I don't save. $20/week is enough to save for a pretty fantastic holiday once a year. 10 day cruise? You can pick those up for $80-100/night if you plan ahead (book 4-5 months in advance, they offer lower rates to secure the ship or something like that. Then when they meet the minimum booking number the price doubles or sometimes triples. I got my parents onto this and they just did 14 days at $75/night per person.) Cruises are fantastic because you don't do fucking anything. No planning attractions, no cleaning or hotels or driving. Get on ship, unpack once, go relax. People clean your room 3 times a day, your meals are cooked, you have a bell boy, your waiter learns your name and your preferences (service personnel on cruises are demi gods I swear). The only thing you pay for after a ticket is grog + activities at destinations you visit. You can do it super cheap if you don't think 'Oh I'm on holiday I have to think about and buy presents for people.' A holiday is for you, fuck them. Send a postcard that'll arrive after you get home. After all, it's the thought that counts right?

  • Being selfish. There is nothing wrong with being selfish in the correct circumstances. In my world I am number 1, even my partners rank below me. Why? Because I do not live other peoples lives I live mine. My happiness comes first. If helping you will negatively impact myself in a way that I cannot recover from in a short time without it having a negative ripple-effect of the rest of my life then guess what, time for you to learn how to deal with your own shit. I'm not a dick, I'll console you if your parents die or be sympathetic if your partner leaves you unexpectedly. But if you cause things to happen to yourself then come to me for sympathy or recourse I will wave you on. I am not an emotional dumpster and no you cannot borrow $500 to pay a fine.
